canonical_name: forward Wilson factorial congruence for natural primes
canonical_statement: For every natural number p, if p is prime, then the factorial of p - 1 is congruent to -1 modulo p, represented as equality in ZMod p.
canonical_claim: For every p : Nat, p.Prime implies that the cast of Nat.factorial (p - 1) into ZMod p equals the additive inverse of one.
domain_and_universes: p : Nat; hp : Nat.Prime p; Nat.factorial (p - 1) cast into ZMod p; equality with (-1 : ZMod p); the closed target is Prop in Lean universe 0.
excluded_degenerate_cases: p = 0, p = 1, and every composite modulus are excluded only because they fail p.Prime. p = 2 is included. No odd-prime side condition is added.
degenerate_case_status: The forward target includes p = 2. Natural truncated subtraction is harmless under p.Prime. The accidental equality in ZMod 1 is outside the root because 1 is not prime and remains relevant only to the uncredited converse or iff characterization.
